title: Could Political Stability Spoil The Spanish Debt Miracle?
gist: Gavekal's Cedric Gemehl argues Spain cut public debt from 119% of GDP (2020) to 101% (2025) despite political paralysis and little consolidation, and that the November 29 election is unlikely to derail it — though a more stable government could paradoxically allow more fiscal slippage than gridlock. (Paywalled teaser only.)

themes.theme: Spain's debt decline and election risk

insights.claim: Spain's public debt has fallen from a pandemic peak of 119% of GDP in 2020 to 101% in 2025, despite higher interest rates and political fragmentation.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Spain's deleveraging supports tighter Bonos-Bund spreads relative to other high-debt euro sovereigns.

insights.claim: The Spanish finance ministry projects public debt falling further to 99.1% of GDP in 2026 and 92.8% by 2030.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Official path implies continued improvement in the debt ratio — the benchmark against which post-election fiscal slippage will be judged.

insights.claim: Spain achieved a large reduction in its public debt ratio with little fiscal consolidation, which is unusual in Europe, implying the decline was driven by growth and inflation rather than austerity.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: If nominal growth, not austerity, drives the debt ratio, a growth slowdown is the main risk to the Spanish debt story.
insights.quote: a spectacular reduction in public debt despite political paralysis and little fiscal consolidation

insights.claim: A change of government in Spain's November 29, 2026 election probably would not derail debt reduction, but greater political stability could paradoxically slow the decline by allowing more fiscal slippage than continued parliamentary gridlock.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Contrarian read for Spanish bonds: a decisive election result could be mildly negative for the fiscal path, since gridlock has acted as a de facto spending brake.
